title: Priority slicing and sandbox path for catalog submissions
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and high-velocity internal requests hit the same model intake channel. This produces long turnaround times for high-priority model additions and inconsistent risk handling for regulated customers. Current catalog onboarding mixes exploratory submissions (research/sandbox) with production-grade requests that require version pinning, auditability, and deprecation controls.

Goal: Define and operationalize a two-track intake and prioritization model: (1) a rapid sandbox track for fast evaluation and short-lived catalog entries and (2) a production track for enterprise-grade onboarding with explicit pinning, eval gates, and deprecation runway. Implement a lightweight priority-slicing rubric so PMs and triage leads can consistently route requests and set SLAs. Deliverables include the intake rubric, sandbox policy, pinning matrix, eval-gate checklist, and a small quick-eval harness for initial smoke tests from customer artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a two-track intake rubric on Confluence with routing examples and flow diagrams
Sandbox track implemented as a distinct form in the intake portal with automated flags for temporary catalog entries
Production track includes fields for requested pinning duration, compliance notes, and required eval test set upload
Triage rubric yields consistent outcome in 5 sample customer requests (≥80% agreement across PM/ENG reviewers)
Quick-eval harness (script + runbook) available in GitHub with CI smoke test that can evaluate a new model in <2 hours
Deprecation runway policy and notification templates ready and integrated into catalog admin console

decisions: Adopted two-track intake (sandbox vs production) with explicit checkboxes and confirmation copy to reduce misclassification
Sandbox entries will be marked ephemeral and auto-expire by default after 30 days with option to extend once evaluated
Production onboarding requires a pinned-version request field plus an eval-gate checklist; no model promoted to production without passing security and quality eval gates

risks: Misrouting of enterprise requests to sandbox could cause compliance exposure; mitigations: UI confirmations + required security fields for production track
Overloading triage with too many fields could increase time-to-first-response; mitigations: progressive disclosure and automation for common cases
Auto-expiration policy might remove promising experimental models; mitigation: extension workflow and retention exceptions for partner agreements
review_feedback: Design review requested: stronger affordance for pinned production models (Marcos)

metrics_success: Time to first triage decision: target sandbox <= 3 business days, production <= 7 business days
% of misrouted submissions (sandbox->production or vice versa): target <2% within first quarter
Time from request to catalog publish for production track: target <= 14 business days for standard requests
implementation_notes: Intake form will set a routing flag that the routing service (ENG-1842) uses to assign to triage queues

Pinning matrix maps requested pin duration (30/90/365 days) to approval level (PM, Head of Product, or CTO)
